title: Recalibrate SLO baselines using historical-weighted profiles and add low-cost alert fallback
author: Maya Zhang
description: Motivation: Current SLO alert baselines are static and tuned at org-level heuristics which leads to frequent noisy paging for tenants with differing request shapes. This PR implements a historical-weighted baseline recalibration that computes per-tenant SLO baselines by combining short-term signal with an exponential-decayed historical profile (watermarking). It also introduces a low-cost alert fallback: when a high-cardinality metric triggers, we automatically attempt a cheap synthetic SLO replay and lightweight span-sampling probe before escalating to full alerting. The goal is to reduce noise and infra cost while preserving correctness and time-to-detect for genuine regressions. Implementation summary: 1) New baseline engine (observability/slo/baseline_engine.go) that ingests token-latency and per-invocation cost rollups and produces a tenant baseline using configurable decay and weight parameters. 2) Drift correction module (observability/slo/drift_correction.go) that detects systematic baseline shifts and applies a conservative correction factor so that we don't overfit to transient spikes. 3) Low-cost fallback controller (observability/alerts/fallback_controller.py) that, upon threshold crossings, triggers a synthetic replay queue and a sampled KV-warmup trace probe; only if both probes indicate degradation do we open full-investigation alerts. 4) Dashboard for operators (dashboards/slo-recalibration-overview.json) and a small docs page (docs/observability/baseline-tuning.md) describing knobs and recommended presets. 5) Integration test harness (tests/slo_replay_integration_test.go) that runs synthetic replays against the staged baseline. Backwards compatibility: Baseline engine exposes a config flag to opt-in per-tenant recalibration; default rollout is off. Rollout plan: 1) Canary tenants via feature flag for three days with tight telemetry and cost limits. 2) Expand to 20% of tenants and collect alert reduction/loss-of-detection metrics. 3) Global enable if false negative rate < 0.3% and alert volume reduced >= 18%. Testing: unit tests for baseline math and drift correction; integration test for replay-based fallback; local perf bench showing <1.5% latency overhead for sampling probes. Monitoring and observability: new metrics slo.baseline.absolute, slo.baseline.delta, slo.fallback.invocations, slo.fallback.probe_success, slo.drift.detected_count; traces instrumented for fallback decision path with span tags fallback.probe.type and fallback.probe.duration. Configuration knobs: decay.window_days, decay.weight_alpha, fallback.probe_timeout_ms, fallback.probe_sample_rate, synthetic_replay_batch. Security/ops: fallback controller runs under observability service account and respects tenant data-scoping; synthetic replay uses masked prompts to avoid PII egress. Related: ENG-3421 (SLO baseline initiative), ENG-3489 (alert volume reduction).
